---
title: "student-qmd.yml"
---

Writes the `.qmd` files a course can hand to students,
from assessment sources that keep each answer beside its question.

A homework or exam whose answers sit in `.sol` divs,
or whose included question fragments carry them,
can never be given out as it stands.
This capability writes a self-contained copy of each source,
proves the copy carries nothing it should not,
and renders it alone the way a student would.

It is ported from `Morrison-Lab/mlg`'s `tools/make_student_qmd.py`
and the `--student-qmd` half of its `tools/check_student_copy.py`,
with the extras `Morrison-Lab/epi204`'s generator needed.

## What it does

For each source, three steps, each able to fail the job:

1. **Write** `<output-dir>/<source file name>`:
   - every `{{< include >}}` is inlined, recursively,
     resolved the way Quarto resolves it:
     a path starting with `/` from the project root,
     and any other path from the directory of the top-level document,
     even inside an included file;
   - an included file's own front matter is dropped.
     Quarto merges it into the document instead,
     so a key other than `filters` gets a warning;
   - every answer-key-only div is removed with everything inside it:
     a div with one of the `hidden-classes`,
     and a `content-visible` or `content-hidden` div
     that Quarto shows only under one of the `answer-profiles`
     or hides under the `student-profile`;
   - HTML comments outside code, and whole-line `#` comments in the front matter,
     are removed, since they carry instructor notes;
   - with `drop-render-chunks`, fenced code blocks that run `quarto render`
     are removed too, with any div they leave empty.

   It fails rather than guess on a missing include, unbalanced divs,
   an unclosed code fence or comment,
   or two sources with the same file name.
2. **Check** each written file against its source with Quarto's own Pandoc
   (`quarto pandoc`), so the check shares no parser with the writer.
   A file fails when it is missing, still has an include,
   has an answer-key-only div, an HTML comment or a front-matter comment,
   or differs in any other way from its source's AST
   with those parts taken out.
   A source div classed `.solution`, `.answer` or the like fails too:
   the assign filter passes such a div through untouched,
   so an answer written in one would reach every student.
3. **Render** each written file alone, in an empty directory outside the repository,
   so anything it still needs from the repository fails here
   rather than on a student's machine.
   A file with executable cells needs their engine (R, Python, ...)
   set up before this runs, or `render: false`.

The defaults match the
[`coatless-quarto/assign`](https://github.com/coatless-quarto/assign) filter:
it hides `.sol` and `.rubric` divs,
and shows them under the `solution`, `solutions` and `rubric` profiles.

## Inputs

| Input | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sources` | string | *(required)* | Source `.qmd` paths or globs (`**` allowed), separated by spaces or newlines. |
| `working-directory` | string | `'.'` | Directory to run in; `sources` and `output-dir` are relative to it. |
| `output-dir` | string | `'_student-qmd'` | Directory to write the student files to, one per source, named as the source. |
| `hidden-classes` | string | `'sol rubric'` | Div classes only the answer key shows. |
| `answer-profiles` | string | `'solution solutions rubric'` | Profiles whose `when-profile` content is answer-key only. |
| `student-profile` | string | `'assign'` | The profile the student copy renders under. |
| `drop-render-chunks` | boolean | `false` | Also remove fenced code blocks that run `quarto render`. |
| `require-answers` | boolean | `true` | Fail a source with no answer-key-only div; when false, warn instead. A run in which no source has one still fails. |
| `check` | boolean | `true` | Check each student file against its source. |
| `render` | boolean | `true` | Render each student file alone in an empty directory. |
| `render-to` | string | `'html'` | Output format for that render. |
| `index-title` | string | `''` | When set, also write an `index.html` in `output-dir` listing the files. |
| `index-back-href` | string | `''` | A back link for that index page. |
| `quarto-version` | string | `'release'` | Quarto version to install. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `checkout-submodules` | boolean | `false` | Initialize the caller's git submodules first (for includes that live in one). |
| `artifact-name` | string | `''` | When set, upload the student files as a workflow artifact with this name. |

The composite action (`Morrison-Lab/gha/student-qmd@v2`)
takes the same inputs except the last two,
plus `install-quarto` (default `'true'`),
and outputs `output-dir` (an absolute path) and `count`.

## Permissions

Needs only `contents: read`, the default,
so the caller needs no `permissions:` block.

## Example

```yaml
name: Student .qmd files

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  student-qmd:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/student-qmd.yml@v2
    with:
      sources: |
        Homework/**/hw*.qmd
        Exams/**/exam*.qmd
      # drop-render-chunks: true      # also drop `quarto render` code blocks
      # require-answers: false        # warn, not fail, on a source with no answers
      # render: false                 # skip rendering (e.g. cells need R)
      # artifact-name: student-qmd    # upload the files
```

To publish the files with a site instead,
call the composite action in the job that builds the site,
with `output-dir` inside the rendered output.

## What stays with the caller

Checks about a whole project's render,
such as how many pages a render produced
or whether every question fragment names the assign filter in its front matter,
are specific to each course repository and are not part of this capability.
